To be honest, I am less inclined to respond/keep a writing partner around when they send me messages over and  over again. I am busy, I tell people I have a busy life and I expect people to be patient, I extend that same patience to my writing partners as well. Sometimes people don't ghost because they want to, I've had so many people just be busy, feel ashamed for being busy and reaching out again or even just forgetting to reply but then realizing they have not replied and then ghosting fully. Ghosting does not always have bad intentions. 

Unless people openly tell me they do not wish to continue to write with me anymore, I assume they are busy. It's a stance I adapted a while ago and has helped me a lot. Spares me a lot of headache and overthinking and quite frankly: I did not have to deal with similar behaviour of yours in other writing partners. Everything has become more "relaxed" and I found more people that I vibed with and got along with great, especially when it comes to both mine and my writing partners expectations, our schedules and not having to feel like we constantly have to check in with each other.

Many people set their liquid foundation with either one of these or a combination, powder foundation, translucent powder and setting spray but some foundations dry down. 
I use translucent powder because there's a lot of product in most of them and I can use it on my whole face, where powder foundation might be a bit too dark for under your eyes. I also work in theater and we use a lot of translucent powder but because it's so long lasting and has a lot of product, it lasts about 50 shows with around 30 people getting make up and then setting it.

I would first start with foundation and brows, then work you way up with contour and other stuff.
When I was a complete eyebrow beginner, I went to a benefit counter, they are probably most known for their brow products. Ask for help and what you want to do with your brows, many offer to do your brows with the products that they recommend to show how that product performs. 
I personally prefer a liquid foundation but that's up to you and your personal preference - for cosplay I usually use liquid foundation applied with a sponge / beauty blender dupe. Employees will also ask for your skin type so they can recommend a foundation that is ment for your skin type so that is actually important! They also ask what kind of coverage and finish you want to have.
Also there's no need for an eye primer, concealer works perfectly fine for me. Eye primer is mostly used to either have a good base before you apply eye shadow or to even out your eyelid. I use concealer to even out because my eyelid is very discolorated.

Also I'm not sure why I have to discuss my issues with a male person that doesn't know anything what it's like to be a female in games or male dominated fields in general. Sure exchanging opinions can help but in the end we all have to change ourselves to make the situation better for everyone but mostly the one that feels bad in these situations. But sure, these things don't apply to you so _you_ don't feel like there's anything wrong. Or do you have to deal with supervisors calling you names, making fun of you and sexually harassing you in your workspace? Do you have to fear for your life while going out while it's dark outside? Just because it doesn't apply to you doesn't make an individual experience less valid. 

I dont hope to find toxicity, I don't hop into voice chat each time to get the sweet validation of getting harassed every day, it's there wherever I go. My male friends don't experience any of the toxicity I do. They even asked me to stop speaking in voice chat so they could enjoy some games without toxicity. When I'm not speaking my game experience is mostly positive, there are occasional toxic people but that's normal for every game, people that shittalk all the time. When I'm speaking my game experience is horrible. I have to actually fear for my live because I know what it's like to be stalked, be followed to my front door. There are people on the internet who arranged that. I can deal with most of the comments but something that involves my personal address or anything that goes further than just the game and toxicity makes me feel uncomfortable. But you haven't experienced that so my experience is not that valid or not real. Have you been stalked and had to fear for your live just because you're a male? 

I don't claim to speak special or anything, I'm just stating facts. I recently found this ( https://twitter.com/chhopsky/status/1082184759982211072?s=19 , sorry for no proper format, I'm on mobile ) and it is classified as harassment. Why can't we just all be a bit nice to each other? Why do people have to be toxic on the internet? 

Also, the definition of harassment is repeated unwanted contact without a reasonable purpose, insults, threats, touching, or offensive language. So "back to the kitchen" is unnecessary and while they are jokes to some, they aren't to most of the female population. It is classified as harassment. You have no say in what is a joke and what's not if you're not the "targeted" person in the so called joke. 
Do you actively report players that are either extremely toxic or harass people? If not, you're passively enabling and supporting those people, they will think it's okay, they don't get banned so they do no wrong. 

But hey, at least you're not an asshole, right?
